name: Introduction and overview — F-22 Raptor — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — F-22 Raptor
description: Introduction and overview of the F-22 Raptor: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The F-22 Raptor is a twin-engine stealth air-superiority fighter built by Lockheed Martin, entering service in 2005. It combines stealth, supercruise (sustained supersonic flight without afterburner, about Mach 1.8), and thrust-vectoring agility. Only 195 were built after production ended in 2011, all for the U.S. Air Force. Baseline facts: Twin-engine stealth air-superiority fighter; USAF service from 2005; 195 built by Lockheed Martin..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: F-22 Raptor: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Twin-engine stealth air-superiority fighter; USAF service from 2005; 195 built by Lockheed Martin.
Key figure: Top speed Mach 2.25; supercruise at Mach 1.8; two Pratt & Whitney F119 turbofans with thrust vectoring.
